name: Mitochondrial Biogenesis and Retrograde Signaling
description: Mitochondrial biogenesis in S. cerevisiae requires coordinated expression of nuclear and mitochondrial genomes, protein import, membrane assembly, and quality control. Under respiratory growth, the transcription factors Hap2/3/4/5 activate nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial proteins. The RTG (retrograde) pathway senses mitochondrial dysfunction and activates compensatory nuclear gene expression via Rtg1/3 transcription factors (inhibited by Mks1 when mitochondria are healthy). Mitochondrial import involves TOM/TIM complexes for protein translocation. The pathway integrates signals from TOR, carbon source, and mitochondrial membrane potential. This illustrates organelle-nucleus communication with high AND gate requirements for complex assembly.
scientificAccuracy: Based on extensive research on yeast mitochondrial biogenesis and retrograde signaling. All components validated.
